newsitem.title: DUBAI: Khashoggi ponders legal action against Thais-paper.
newsitem.headline: Khashoggi ponders legal action against Thais-paper.

text.p: Saudi Arabian tycoon Adnan Khashoggi was quoted on Thursday as saying he was considering suing authorities in Thailand for defamation but did not plan to go to Bangkok to try to disprove fraud charges against him.
He made his comments in an interview with the Saudi newspaper Al-Eqtisadiah.

The paper said the interview took place in Paris on Wednesday, the day Thai police said they had issued another arrest warrant for Khashoggi on a separate charge of conspiring to defraud the ailing Bangkok Bank of Commerce.

They said Khashoggi was wanted for conspiring with five other suspects to defraud the bank of 260 million baht ($10 million). Earlier this month police issued an arrest warrant for Khashoggi on a charge of conspiring with five others to obtain two billion baht in loans from the bank.
"I am still waiting patiently for an amicable settlement," Khashoggi said, adding that he would start legal action if that was not achieved by early next week.

Asked what he would do if a settlement was not reached, he said: "Then I will find myself forced to file a lawsuit...against the board of directors of the Bangkok Bank of Commerce...and the Thai Central Bank."

"My dealings with the bank took place in an official way. I did not invest my money in projects (in Thailand) to get into trouble...I might ask for financial compensation for slander, defamation and causing losses because the stoppage of my business with banks and companies was a result of that (the charges)," Khashoggi said.

Asked if he would go to Thailand as the Thai police suggested to disprove the charges, he said: "...It is just a ploy to get me into Thailand so they can arrest me, in which case I will lose the chance to defend myself."

"I am in the process of sending a memo to the Thai prime minister with all the details of my relations with the bank from the start to the recent developments. I will also ask the Thai authorities to present me with full details on the issue and the accusations against me," Khashoggi said.
He said he was presenting the letter to the Thai embassy in Paris on Wednesday.

Bangkok Bank of Commerce, saddled with bad loans of more than 70 billion baht, was taken over by the government last year after opposition party charges about the debts triggered a run on its deposits.
